judgment.reason: The central translation lemma does not validly establish that f is affine on a tail. Constant-difference relations only for offsets obtained from the parameters do not, without further argument or regularity, imply an affine formula on an interval.
The claimed “standard translation argument” and subsequent inference from constant increments to tail affinity are not proved and are not justified under the stated assumptions.
Its key step—tail translation identities imply f(t)=ct+d on a tail—is asserted without a valid derivation. No regularity assumption permits this conclusion directly.
The tail-translation lemma is only described informally and does not prove tail affinity. Iterating fixed-offset identities does not by itself yield an affine function on a real interval.
